title: Wealthy Daughter Murder Case
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, Inspector Megure) omitted by convention. Ran's near-drowning in the kitchen has no node on the other end since she's omitted -- captured as attrs on Ichieda's node plus a location-directed edge to the kitchen instead of a person-to-person edge. Correcting the v1 scaffold: it listed only Nikaido as a victim, but Reika Yotsui herself is also murdered (drowned in a rigged, slow-filling bathtub) -- both are added as victim nodes, since both are revealed to be the culprit's real, deliberately chosen targets from the same two-years-ago backstory, not a random spree as the killer tries to make it look. The 'random murders' framing and the kitchen attack on an arbitrary guest are the misdirection the killer engineers on purpose; has_motive_against is real (not a red herring) for both named victims, while Mifune and Rokuda's lack of alibi for the 5-6 AM window is the episode's actual red herring, captured as red-herring implicates edges rather than fabricated motives neither of them is shown to have. case_type: murder.

clues.desc: Trying to run a bath in the lodge's bathroom produces water from the shower head instead of the faucet -- the killer used the shower to quietly, slowly fill the tub around a bound victim rather than the faucet, which would have finished (and been noticed) too quickly.

Reika disappeared at 10:00 PM but wasn't killed until between 5:00 and 6:00 AM the next morning -- a seven-to-eight-hour gap inconsistent with a quick, opportunistic crime, pointing instead to a deliberately timed, delayed-drowning setup. Since only Mifune and Rokuda lack an alibi for that narrow window, suspicion initially falls on them.

All the air conditioners' timers are still set to 12:30, and Conan recalls hearing a bell right after the blackout -- the lodge's dial-type microwaves kept turning without power and were still warm to the touch afterward. Together these prove the power outage was a deliberately engineered overload timed in advance, not an outside intruder cutting the line.

Water blotches appear on all three men's clothes, but Gojo's are on his sleeves from washing his hands and Mifune's are on his collar from washing his face -- Ichieda's are on his rolled-up-sleeve elbows, a pattern that only makes sense if he pulled a soaking, submerged body out of the tub with his coat off.

The attack on the drugged, randomly-affected guest in the kitchen initially reads as proof of an indiscriminate, motiveless killer loose in the lodge -- but its only real function is to put a first-hand account of "my head was held underwater" on record, manufacturing false testimony that ties Reika's and Nikaido's deaths to the same MO in witnesses' minds.
